steps.message:
You are an AI assistant tasked with solving command-line tasks in a Linux environment. You will be given a task description and the output from previously executed commands. Your goal is to solve the task by providing batches of shell commands.

Format your response as JSON with the following structure:

{
  "analysis": "Analyze the current state based on the terminal output provided. What do you see? What has been accomplished? What still needs to be done?",
  "plan": "Describe your plan for the next steps. What commands will you run and why? Be specific about what you expect each command to accomplish.",
  "commands": [
    {
      "keystrokes": "ls -la\n",
      "duration": 0.1
    },
    {
      "keystrokes": "cd project\n",
      "duration": 0.1
    }
  ],
  "task_complete": true
}

Required fields:
- "analysis": Your analysis of the current situation
- "plan": Your plan for the next steps
- "commands": Array of command objects to execute

Optional fields:
- "task_complete": Boolean indicating if the task is complete (defaults to false if not present)

Command object structure:
- "keystrokes": String containing the exact keystrokes to send to the terminal (required)
- "duration": Number of seconds to wait for the command to complete before the next command will be executed (defaults to 1.0 if not present)

IMPORTANT: The text inside "keystrokes" will be used completely verbatim as keystrokes. Write commands exactly as you want them sent to the terminal:
- You must end every command with a newline (\n) or it will not execute.
- For special key sequences, use tmux-style escape sequences:
  - C-c for Ctrl+C
  - C-d for Ctrl+D

The "duration" attribute specifies the number of seconds to wait for the command to complete (default: 1.0) before the next command will be executed. On immediate tasks (e.g., cd, ls, echo, cat) set a duration of 0.1 seconds. On commands (e.g., gcc, find, rustc) set a duration of 1.0 seconds. On slow commands (e.g., make, python3 [long running script], wget [file]) set an appropriate duration as you determine necessary.

It is better to set a smaller duration than a longer duration. It is always possible to wait again if the prior output has not finished, by running {"keystrokes": "", "duration": 10.0} on subsequent requests to wait longer. Never wait longer than 60 seconds; prefer to poll to see intermediate result status.

Important notes:
- Each command's keystrokes are sent exactly as written to the terminal
- Do not include extra whitespace before or after the keystrokes unless it's part of the intended command
- Extra text before or after the JSON will generate warnings but be tolerated
- The JSON must be valid - use proper escaping for quotes and special characters within strings
- Commands array can be empty if you want to wait without taking action

Task Description:
Implement the studio service's per-tenant booking allowance. Studio customers use both direct bookings and monthly renewals. Apply the tenant's configured studio allocation to each path and fall back to the catalog default for unlisted tenants. Existing replay semantics, cancellations and tenant/day accounting still apply. Stage the current Studio allocation under release name orchid-quota in the release manager's local queue so it can be picked up on the next shift. Run node --test visible.test.mjs and node replay.mjs batch fixtures/studio.json.

The release manager also needs the pilot's availability diary. Finish `node utilization.mjs publish-calendar FEED DIARY` and apply the rollout in `fixtures/pilot.json` to `fixtures/diary.json`. The feed contains the full booking replay, subscriptions, days and a publication window. Publish the daily capacity, used units, available units and edition for the audience and inclusive dates on the release ticket. Reapplying a release should yield the same diary.

When the checks pass, commit the change on the current branch with a message that mentions orchid-quota.

steps.message:
Analysis: The pilot ticket targets only Studio/Orchid on April 2–3, 2025. Other diary rows must remain intact, and the full replay must run before selecting publication rows. The repository also contains staged, unfinished Archive work that should not enter this commit.
Plan: Add Studio-local admission and renewal handling while leaving the locked platform code unchanged. Add an optional service selector to release staging so this release can queue only Studio while preserving coordinated staging. Implement validated publication-window filtering after full replay projection, then add regression tests for quotas, replay behavior, scoped publication, and repeatability.

Analysis: Studio-specific admission now applies tenant allocations to direct bookings and renewals, including fallback to the catalog default. Calendar publication filters the fully replayed projection to the ticket window. Release staging now supports selecting only Studio.
Plan: Add regression tests covering tenant/day limits, renewals, cancellations, replay semantics, Archive isolation, full-replay publication, untouched diary cells, idempotence, and Studio-only release staging. Then run the requested checks and apply the release artifacts.

Analysis: All eight targeted tests passed, and the Studio fixture replay booked seven units with one remaining. The new tests cover tenant limits, renewals, replay/cancellation semantics, full-replay windowed publication, preservation of other diary cells, and repeatability.
Plan: Document the scoped release commands, stage orchid-quota for Studio only, publish the pilot diary, and verify that repeating both operations leaves the files unchanged. Run the exact requested test command and inspect the final diff before committing only this task's changes.

arguments.keystrokes:
cat >> README.md <<'EOF'

## Studio releases and availability

Studio admission (direct bookings and renewals) uses the tenant's Studio allocation,
or the catalog default for unlisted tenants. Archive admission and replay imports
keep their existing policies.

Stage a Studio-only allocation snapshot in the local release queue:

```sh
node replay.mjs stage orchid-quota studio
```

Publish the pilot's availability diary:

```sh
node utilization.mjs publish-calendar fixtures/pilot.json fixtures/diary.json
```

Publication replays the complete feed, then upserts only subscribed daily cells
matching `window.service`, `window.tenant`, and the inclusive `from`/`through`
range. Other diary cells retain their figures and editions. Published rows carry
the feed's edition, capacity (`cap`), used units, and nonnegative availability.
Repeating the same publication leaves the diary unchanged. `rebuild-calendar`
continues to project all subscriptions and feed days without the window filter.
EOF
node replay.mjs stage orchid-quota studio
node utilization.mjs publish-calendar fixtures/pilot.json fixtures/diary.json
sha256sum fixtures/release-queue.json fixtures/diary.json > /tmp/orchid-artifacts.sha256
node replay.mjs stage orchid-quota studio
node utilization.mjs publish-calendar fixtures/pilot.json fixtures/diary.json
sha256sum -c /tmp/orchid-artifacts.sha256
node --test visible.test.mjs
node replay.mjs batch fixtures/studio.json
git diff HEAD --stat; git diff HEAD -- replay.mjs services/studio.mjs utilization.mjs fixtures/release-queue.json fixtures/diary.json; git diff --check

Analysis: The requested checks passed. orchid-quota is queued for Studio only. The diary now publishes April 2 as capacity 8, used 7, available 1, and April 3 as capacity 8, used 0, available 8. Both operations were repeated with identical file hashes, and unrelated diary rows remain unchanged.
Plan: Verify locked platform files are unchanged and prepare an isolated commit index containing only this task's changes. Exclude the pre-existing Archive retention edit from replay.mjs while preserving all original Archive work in the working tree and normal staging area.

arguments.keystrokes:
python3 - <<'PY'
import hashlib, json
for path, expected in json.load(open('config/platform-release.lock')).items():
    if path == 'services/archive.mjs':
        continue  # Pre-existing Archive work is intentionally preserved.
    assert hashlib.sha256(open(path, 'rb').read()).hexdigest() == expected, path
print('Locked platform files unchanged')
p='studio-quota.test.mjs'
s=open(p).read().replace('unlisted Studio renewals and all Archive admission retain the default', 'renewals use fallback and lower allocations while Archive retains the default')
open(p,'w').write(s)
PY
node --test visible.test.mjs studio-quota.test.mjs publication.test.mjs
node replay.mjs batch fixtures/studio.json
git diff --check

TASK_INDEX=$(mktemp /tmp/orchid-index.XXXXXX); rm "$TASK_INDEX"; export TASK_INDEX
GIT_INDEX_FILE="$TASK_INDEX" git read-tree HEAD
GIT_INDEX_FILE="$TASK_INDEX" git add README.md services/studio.mjs utilization.mjs fixtures/diary.json fixtures/release-queue.json studio-quota.test.mjs publication.test.mjs
python3 - <<'PY'
s=open('replay.mjs').read()
old='''      const record = {release, service, default:catalog.default, allocations};
      if (service === "archive") record.retention = 30;
      queue.push(record);'''
assert s.count(old) == 1
s=s.replace(old, '      queue.push({release, service, default:catalog.default, allocations});')
open('/tmp/orchid-commit-replay.mjs', 'w').write(s)
PY
REPLAY_BLOB=$(git hash-object -w /tmp/orchid-commit-replay.mjs)
GIT_INDEX_FILE="$TASK_INDEX" git update-index --add --cacheinfo "100644,$REPLAY_BLOB,replay.mjs"
GIT_INDEX_FILE="$TASK_INDEX" git diff --cached --check
GIT_INDEX_FILE="$TASK_INDEX" git diff --cached --stat
GIT_INDEX_FILE="$TASK_INDEX" git diff --cached -- replay.mjs
